newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW-French consumer spending falls in Feb.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-French consumer spending falls in Feb.

text.p: Following are economists' comments after national statistics institute INSEE said French consumer spending on manufactured goods fell 1.7 percent in February after an upwardly revised rise of 3.0 percent in January (compared to 1.9 percent rise initially announced)
SEAN SHEPLEY, ECONOMIST, CS FIRST BOSTON
The big problem is a seasonal one. We had a substantial revision to the January numbers with a big increase. Overall, it's consistent with a recovery in demand after a weak fourth quarter.

The February fall is bigger than expected, but there is a strong revision in January. The January figures are up because of the January sales. Overall there is nothing surprising in these figures. It shows households are more sensitive to the effects of sales. We have to wait until March and April, when the sales effect ceases to be a factor.

Obviously the fact it's sliding is not a good thing. Any figure below 58 billion (francs) is disappointing in terms of French consumption. Optimism is in the air but we are not seeing it on the ground. The figures are consistent with our forecast of 1997 GDP growth of just under two percent.
